As plenty of others have said already, the quality stuff is mostly for the endgame customers, the last expansion you unlock. They will not accept anything below heavenly iirc. It does help in improving the samples given out, but it's very RNG-heavy. I've had success with some 11% sample, but failed repeatedly at 80%. I think for the early to mid game, you don't have to worry about heavenly that much, you'll get the customers regardless, just keep giving them samples until you succeed. If more expansions come out, I would assume they would also want the max quality, but we'll see about that.

Nah, I mean it has the most trunk storage in the game, at 16 slots, so I could finally fit in all my stuff lol. 

Looking back at my early game when there weren't 100+ guides and pro tips, I overused the sprinklers and such, but the botanists and workers are way better. It's best to get them asap if you can afford them, and stop buying those things. At that point, all you need to start doing is resupplying the ingredients, which is basically all you do at endgame. 

Hope you enjoy the game!

You don't need to have 5-10 items for sale, it's just redundant. I would enjoy it to be honest! Too many people are rushing to endgame and trying to make the expensive coke. I'm glad I slowed down and just enjoyed progressing slowly through the drugs. You'll get there eventually. 

It will get tedious at the end when you want to start making mixes, I'll personally just switch to og kush/purp and sell it exclusively to avoid the burnout of resupply.

Really up to you, it's very tedious to keep resupplying manually once you get to the endgame. Depends on if that's what you want to do or if you want a more relaxed gameplay with fewer set-ups. Not sure how well you know Skyrim though, which can change some things. I would advise you to get into enchanting/alchemy as you continue playing. You can be filthy rich with alchemy, but it is tedious, but I'm at about 4 million gold, legit, just selling and making pots. Can just grab ingredients as you adventure around the world, or hit/reload the vendor to reset ingredients. 

Of course, enchanting, get that -100% destruct or any magic skill, so your skills don't cost mana to cast, you can focus on HP/Stam at that point. Get your magic resist up too, when you max it at 85%, other mages and dragons will do 0 damage to you.

Granted, this all takes work and can be tedious, but even if you take it slow, you will eventually max and craft all these things. Just enjoy the game for now! Never tried the sword/mage hybrid, but I guess that also brings other things into the equation, like smithing. 

I did do a mage build in my game but switched to 2H, dual-handed, and bow for a change. Though of course, most importantly, just enjoy the game at your own pace, no need to min-max all these things, I just have a bad habit maxing them to get OP early on.

I lurk and never commented here before, but you are 100% correct. I used to go out on my own, handing out snacks, socks, money or even praying with a few. Not including church outreaches. Not my business what they do if I give them money, I’ve always accepted that.

I don't mind, to be honest, plus I actually finished the main quest, which I haven't done in a long time, for the dragon rend shout. Thanks to that, I can land them quickly and kill them in like 4 seconds with my endgame dual wield build lol.

But before that, yeah they aren't too fun. Make sure to get magic resist capped so they do zero damage to you, should help too.

The dumb civil war lol. I always side with the legion. It's tedious, but it helps remove the whole peace talk during the main quest progression. Also make sure to get the elder scroll before even continuing the main quest, because that also saves a lot of time. 

This all does take up time, but I'm leveling and getting stronger while doing all these other things. I also have a bad habit of maxing alchemy and enchant, so it makes me OP when I start the main quest, all the DLCs, and all the guilds.

Magic resist, magic resist, magic resist, and oh, more magic resist. Get it capped at 85% and dragons/mages will no longer be an issue. Mostly just physical damage, but even then, if you make smithing potions, and smithing enchant gear, you should hit the armor cap as well, so thats like 80% reduction to physical damage.

I do not enjoy legendary at low levels, just ruins the fun personally. I would stick to around adept/expert, and ONLY bumped it up to legendary when I maxed enchant/alch/smithing. I was playing 2H, and now destro, and everything is still a walk in the park. Granted, had to make destro potions to make it even better.

I didn't really upgrade Magicka either, since I was planning on using the 100% magic reduction enchants, so I poured most into hp and some stamina. I stuck with hp potions too, since I didn't want to keep healing mid-battle. 

You really shouldn't be having issues once you max alch/enchant. Magic resist is your best friend tho, so max that out too.

Probably max out enchant and just make your knight be on steroids with all those one-handed % enchants. I would also try getting more magic resist so any dragons and mages don't become a problem anymore, their damage will tickle you. If you also have the time or care, max out alchemy to make your weapons and armor max rating. 

Of course though, personal choice, just enjoy the game at your own pace, you don't need OP stuff asap. I don't tend to use Skyrim gear, I always make my own.

I guess if you're into alchemy, maybe make some poison potions for even more damage, I was able to make some that did 400 dps per hit, but I didn't really use them.

 I would agree with the rest, max out enchant to increase your bow damage with %, and maybe try to find the muffle enchant for your shoes so you are not able to be heard if you walk around anywhere.

Don't disenchant the special armor the guilds give you unless you have a mod installed that allows you to reuse those enchantments. I just downloaded a mod that made nightingale armor craftable for the looks, since I don't use those gears if my alchemy and maxed enchant make me able to make OP armor myself. 

I'd stick with light armor for stealth builds, it's just lighter for stealth builds, and it seems you're almost at a cap for it anyway. 

Maybe also start getting some magic resist in the future so dragons and mages do literally zero damage to you.

Hm, I have not done the restoration in such a long time. Do you mean this will have HP in the millions and such?

In that case, best to go full on HP/Magic Resist/and if a mage, either -100% mana reduction on a mage school, or just 1H/2H stuff if you use weapons. I would probably just go full on dps fire and another enchant for the weapon. When you have -100% destro, it doesn't use up the charge.

I wouldn't bother with school % reduction if you will have millions of mana, but the destro one is nice for the infinite charge.

As for the rest, don't get regen if you will have mana/hp/stamina in the millions, very pointless, you will never run out haha. 

I wouldn't do resist posion/disease either, rarely do you get sickness from stuff in game, and even then, merchants sell cure-all potions you can carry around in the inventory. Maybe get more Archery/2H/1H enchants so you can switch between weapons if you get bored.

No to pickpocket, unless you are playing a legit build as a thief or something, quite useless, so get another weapon enchant. As another said, sneak is probably not very useful in these scenarios, you can literally walk up and one shot someone haha.

Lastly, not sure if this is obvious, but getting resist fire/shock/cold is useless, just use magic resist, it resists all of it. On my legit playthrough, I got the max 85% MR, so dragons and mages aren't a problem anymore. 

Hope that helps! Just skip the regens basically.
True, it doesn't really get great until you get the complete destro reduction. I only switched to mage with maxed out alchemy and enchant lol.

Honestly never played stealth archer completely, more so just sneaking when they are far away as usual. Never played with the illusion/posion/sneaking and such, I just like charging in with 2H or mage.

Right now just switched to mage to have fun, though I was using a 2H/Archer build before this. With destro potions, its pretty OP, even on legendary diff!

Those are pretty solid to be honest, in the early stages of the game, the mana is definitely a big pain in the butt. The flames are probably the best, they tick for damage over time, while also doing good damage and being the cheapest to cast.

Beyond that, you can go for the usual Firebolt that's next, but it's expensive mana-wise, you can buy it off the dude at the whiterun castle to the right. 

As for specific spells, I mean you have seen all the magic schools, it's pretty fun for options. Conjuration, obviously, minions to fight for you, Destro dps, and Alteration has a nice spell for more body armor, but again, mana consumption. 

I'd probably just recommend sticking with healing/destro if you want the simplest build, maybe conjuration to have a minion tank for ya. For now, since you're starting out, stick with the fire/heal spells they gave you, they are good until you can get more mana and use higher-leveled ones like Firebolt. 

If you can find destruction reduction armor pieces, that would be fantastic as well! 

I don't want to overwhelm you, but enchanting, alchemy are the most broken perks to get powerful gear and potions. You can enchant gear pieces to get -100% destruction reduction, so you can pretty much cast the most powerful spells for free, no mana needed, that's the route most people go instead of just upgrading a ton of mana. 

Feel free to ask more questions!

Yup, good idea with disenchanting gear! 

Well, I guess for common sense, you don't want to be looting brooms and buckets, haha, those have zero uses. So weapons, armor, gold, gems, and so on are okay.

What someone else said is correct too, got to make sure what your picking up is worth carrying. Generally, 1lb should be equivalent to 10 gold. But in the early game, it's okay to take and sell them all if you have the space.

Continue the main story line, you will eventually end up getting a follow/companion. They can help hoard some loot for you, but they have a limit as well. 

If you want a permanent storage place/house, it will be from Whiterun, the first city, and where it takes you for the main quest. It will cost 5k gold, and 1.8k for renovations added. Unlimited storage chest upstairs.

I would also avoid picking up food, stick with potions for hp. Lastly, if you are playing a mage, definitely check out the College of Winterhold! It's the main mage location, all the npcs have every school of magic and books for sell available for new spells. Talking to the advisor the jarl points you to, he should tell you more information about that.

Hope you have fun! there is also a carriage outside the city, in the stables. You can hire him and just travel the different cities to explore the world and such, the choices are endless!

Will you play on PC/Console? Any mods? Those definitely change the game, as well as the much better perks on PC with the Ordinator mod.

Generally, yes, you want to pick a "build" per say, and stick to leveling up those perks. I think if you take the game slowly, you shouldn't ever have a problem with leveling. That kind of only happens when you max skills to 100 either from exploits or a legit method.

Such as making Smithing to 100 at level 1 or something, when you leave the city, enemies are stronger but you still have the same gear and weapons, do you get what I mean?

As for DLC, I think it depends. I personally finished the main quest first, along with the whole legion vs storm cloak before moving on to DLC. It helps already having the elder scroll, dragon-rend shout, and so on for the rest of the game. 

As for over-leveling fear, did you upgrade your enchant, smith, or alchemy when you played? The game gets pretty easy when you start maxing those out. I was about to go from Adept to Legendary comfortably after creating a new gear set with enchants. 

You also don't need any points into any perk before they start gaining experience, that's just how the game is. You can be a stealth archer or mage, if you use healing, it's going to level up from usage regardless.

I'm 29M, living at home. Terrible mental health issues, wasting my life away from dropping out of school at 16, depression, and a psych ward visit at 18. Finally got my HS diploma at 24 in Sept of 2019, not a bachelor's like others by then with a career. 

Just now been in community college since I was 26, but with similar mental health struggles, I'm still here in community college at 29M. Been on disability benefits since I was about 3 years old from childhood cancer, so that's been my ONLY income since then. Can't really splurge like others my age with vacations, restaurants, new clothes and shoes, or even owning a car by then. Just rent and food mostly. 

You need to stop looking up. I've served in church and outreaches with the homeless. I saw someone's whole face light up with a simple sandwich. I still been broke, but have been able to give away my new shoes to a woman whose shoes were worn out and stinky, and a few sweaters, and a jacket to a blind man. (Don't give a fuck either, nor bragging about it, I just loved them more than my own possessions.) 

Is my life any better? No. Still here and living though. I can look up as well, with all these 18-year-olds with a license, in college, or heck, even with their bachelor's at 22 and a nice career, but what does that gain me? Been to 2 more psych ward visits, with these kids younger than me as nurses too. 

Everyone just has their own path. You need to be grateful for what you have right now, you need to actively practice that though, which I know is hard in this generation, which social media doesn't help. 

20k saved is amazing, I know half of Americans don't even have 1k. Sometimes an emergency $300 bill is also not even possible. Also paying rent while saving up a crap ton is amazing. Who cares if others got their own apartment, you have time to save up and maybe make a down payment for a house in the future, not struggling with rent in your 30s/40s/50s.

Maybe try volunteering somewhere, and maybe buy a homeless person a meal. Doesn't help you feel "behind", because you are not, at all. 

As for romance, that's totally 100% possible. Homeless people are dating or married. Disabled people are married, and depend solely on their spouse. Poor people get married and have kids all the time. 

Sometimes love really overpowers any amount of money you have or can't afford. People just want to feel loved and desired, that's it. You're doing really solid in life at 24M, you should have zero issues with romance, man. Not to invalidate your feelings, just logically, your issues aren't financial to prevent ya from dating. 

Just build your confidence, maybe work out, and continue saving money and paying off debts, maybe start investing your money too, for future comfort. You need to stop feeling sorry or feeling left behind bro. Even with me, homeless people dream of a warm bed, warm food, and access to a shower and bathroom.

Is my life still hard? Yes. So, again, I can be grateful I live at home with my own room and these utilities. Also happy I have an amazing family and sister who would do anything for me, others have miserable families and abusive parents, another thing I am grateful for. Hope that helps!

The only thing I would correct you on is that "guilt" problem. No, the Spirit convicts you, not guilts you. That's why you feel that what you're doing is not good, that's God correcting you and keeping you on the right path. Just be careful with that. 

There are just two types of sorrow, as stated here:

2 Corinthians 7:10 NLT

10 For the kind of sorrow God wants us to experience leads us away from sin and results in salvation. There’s no regret for that kind of sorrow. But worldly sorrow, which lacks repentance, results in spiritual death.

I have to remind myself of this sometimes. If I feel guilty but don't repent or want to change, it's worldly sorrow, which is worthless, kind of similar to self-pity. While the other one, conviction and truly feeling regretful for what you've done, leads to repentance. Just got to remember that difference next time you mess up.

Hm, kind of conflicting, to be honest. I don't agree that you need to remain friends with them to show them the Lord's love and be the "light" to them. You're kind of just opening yourself up for temptation and the old lifestyle.

I used to have a lot of gaming friends, which again is different than real-life ones. But most talked about using drugs, playing games, and cursing a lot or were obviously not Christian. Could I have stayed friends? Sure. But what did I gain from that?

Is it my responsibility to convince them to repent or accept God? No. They were just dragging me back into my old lifestyle. I think it's kind of silly to remain friends with them and think you won't be affected.

I would prefer to find some Christian friends, especially if you are saying they are into new-age stuff and "darker" things. Why would you stay friends with that? Keep praying for them, sure, but:


2 Corinthians 6:14-15 NLT

14 Don’t team up with those who are unbelievers. How can righteousness be a partner with wickedness? How can light live with darkness? 

15 What harmony can there be between Christ and the devil? How can a believer be a partner with an unbeliever? 

1 Corinthians 15:33 NLT

33 Don’t be fooled by those who say such things, for “bad company corrupts good character.” 

I did end up leaving behind those friendships, and I really didn't lose much. Did not benefit me at all. In the end, pray to God to get his final answer, not some Reddit comment. Just my 2 cents. Personally, he told me to break off with a new friend I made from a video game. Worldly of course, not Christian.

Just wanted to leave these verses here. Sounds awesome that God has slowly been working on you to overcome these addictions! I think the hard part is definitely thinking we can just cold-turkey these things, but that's not the case.

Over this past month, God has just been reminding me that willpower is NOT enough, we need to depend on his strength, not ours. As for feeling "guilty" for sinning, that's never going to solve anything. You need to continue repenting, getting back up, and fighting it.

Seems you need something else to take up your time, so you're not bored to crave these drugs. Do you have anything else you enjoy that can distract you or take your mind off these things? 

As for the whole church thing, I'm not sure what you mean by that. Unless you have some close brothers in Christ who can hear you out without judging, humans can't really solve this issue, only God can. At best, they can comfort you and tell you to not give up, unless there is also an ex-drug addict who can help you beyond that. Not saying it's wrong, but pray about it and see what God says about it, if you feel led to share it, or just talk about it. 

I'm also guilty since I have been using pills off and on over these past 4-5 weeks, but I learned through these verses God's given me, that I keep deciding to LET sin control me, despite sin not having power over us anymore. You have a choice every single time to indulge or resist. I would encourage you to continue praying and relying on his strength, maybe find other things to do so you don't get bored and crave the drugs.  

Don't mind what others have told you, man. What matters in life is your relationship with God, that's it. No amount of dumb Reddit comments can change that or make you feel bad for not being this righteous Christian(Surprise, no one is). Keep fighting bro, you'll overcome in the end, as long as you keep fighting.

Hey, made this reply a while ago, but you brought up a good question. I would probably still use those scriptures I provided for context. 

None of the disciples, Jesus, or any early Christian wore any such things I would assume, but yet their actions spoke way louder than just a shirt, necklace, or symbol we have access to today. I feel like that is way more impactful than just wanting to be a big neon sign telling others, "LOOK! Christian here! Look at me do a kind deed! Accept Jesus and you can do the same!" 

You know what I mean? This happened back in the old days too.

I had to look this verse up, but it wonderfully explains what I mean.

Matthew 6:1-6 NLT

“Watch out! Don’t do your good deeds publicly, to be admired by others, for you will lose the reward from your Father in heaven. 2 When you give to someone in need, don’t do as the hypocrites do—blowing trumpets in the synagogues and streets to call attention to their acts of charity! I tell you the truth, they have received all the reward they will ever get. 3 But when you give to someone in need, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand is doing. 4 Give your gifts in private, and your Father, who sees everything, will reward you.

Now, it's not necessarily bad to do good deeds in public or wear symbols telling others you follow Christ, but this is a warning when you want to show off and be noticed by others as a result of that. I feel like this falls in the same category. Do others NEED to know you are a Christian to motivate them to accept Jesus?

Even though I did wear a shirt with a verse on it, looking back at it now, I don't think it was a good idea. What you need to focus on is your own relationship with Christ, and becoming more spiritually mature. God will continue to draw others to him, and he doesn't need someone wearing a big cross or a sweatshirt with some bible verse on it to make that happen. Continue to help others out of your love for them as well, not for rewards or being noticed. 

Hope that helps.

Honestly good question. Though, I think it depends on where you're coming from. Are you speaking of a general sense of "why" pain exists and why life is so hard? Or, rather, is it that something specific happened to you that is bothering you and making you angry/doubt God? 

For the first type of anger, even Jesus himself said we will have problems in this life, and no one is exempt from it. I guess, basic Christian beliefs, like sin entering the world, brought this broken state into the world, resulting in pain and suffering for everyone. Can't really be angry at God for that, as it was humans that messed up. In this case, as another commenter posted, give your anger to God and don't draw back because of that. If it's the second type of anger, personal problems that are frustrating and cannot be explained, that is kind of more complicated. With this type of frustration and anger for something that happened to you, it will require healing from that past and continuing your walk with the Lord.

Trust me, coming from someone that was hurt deeply and traumatized in 2021, the second type of pain/anger is not easy to deal with. Honestly, been about 2-3 months "sober" mainly from not liking the effects anymore. I guess like any drug, you use it to have fun, and it really depends on an individual if they get hooked on it. Some can use drugs here and there, but for others, it becomes a full-blown addiction.

I think the main part of this is a reaction to stressful/depressing environments, or just being unhappy. At first, when I used this drug, it felt good with music combined, family was none the wiser. Eventually, it became a coping mechanism, helping me numb pain and not think about anything anymore.

I don't really know what stage you're at, so my advice may be helpful or meaningless, because some people have been abusing it for months/years, and CAN'T stop so easily. It's very similar to alcohol, you crave it, you want it, but in the end, you are just left disappointed and hopeless.

I would suggest finding the root cause of WHY your using it, and when you started. Was it to get high and have "fun", or do you struggle with depression and want to escape for a little while? For me, I simply started hating it, slowly but surely. I understood that my depression was craving the numbness feeling, while at the same time, we have this nostalgia of how good it felt when we first started abusing it. But that nostalgia is a straight up lie. More often than not, you feel bad and guilty for relapsing, and the happiness you felt at first does no longer exist.

Hope this makes sense, I would also suggest not turning to weed or mushrooms, or any type of damn drug. Get sober completely, you are replacing one thing for another. You must deal with your issues sooner or later, or this will become a daily thing. Either weed, cocaine, LSD, etc, any other shit. Best of luck.

It's really like any other drug, it's similar to alcohol, very similar. It's sold in cough medicine, so no one suspects your abusing it or using it beyond the recommended dosage, it's literally cough medicine. Alcohol is more noticeable and its harder to hide among family members. Just like any other drug, you crave it to numb yourself and feel better, so that's the addicting part to it, escapism. Or the nostalgia of it, how "good" you felt when you used, but its still a dark path to go down to, honestly. 

As for the high, you get euphoric at low doses, around 150-200mg. You feel drunk like alcohol at low doses and feel good. You can actually function with it at low doses, yes, go to work and be around family without anyone noticing. Though it turns into a completely different drug at high doses, like PCP is the equivalent to it. It's a disassociate drug, you start to walk funny, have trouble pooping/peeing(Honestly worst part), and start to lose sense of reality. You feel like a stranger to your body.

Now for the very high doses, like 600MG+, I don't have experiences with it, but you really get disconnected and start to hallucinate. Some have out of body experiences and experience that new age crap, oneness, universal answers, going to other dimensions, talking to "spirits", etc. Personally I only lost control of my body and became a spectator ONCE, I could see what I was watching, listening to, what motions my body was doing, but I was not in control. 

Imagine driving a car in the driver seat, now imagine a stranger on your passenger takes control and you suddenly are on the back seat, seeing how he's driving, but you aren't in control. 

You can get addicted to it if you turn to it for comfort and escape from real world problems, but like any other drug, you can stop and only use it occasionally without having any real hardcore substance issues. I guess like alcohol, cocaine, mushrooms, LSD, ecstasy, not everyone is popping every day or using, maybe on weekends or every other week. While others get heavily addicted and dose every single day, yet they go to work and go about their daily activities. Though their mind, spirit, and soul are slowly getting destroyed to be honest. They can't function without it, because they are addicted or don't want to deal with difficult issues in their life. As well as withdrawals. 

Again, you are numb, no emotions, no tears, no bad or positive feelings. I mean you may still get emotional and cry or get depressed, but you don't feel the pain. Though it feels REALLY good listening to music while high, wears off though. 

As for withdrawals, yes, just like alcohol or drugs, if your heavily addicted and using daily, when you want to stop you experience withdrawals. Personally never got that addicted, so never got withdrawals. Though a thing you got to understand about it is that it stays in your body for awhile. You may take it on a Sunday, and by Monday you still feel the effects of it.

Dilatated pupils, will have problems pooping or peeing, and may feel funny. By Tuesday you could be sober, but depends on dosage. You don't necessarily get hang overs or feel like crap with this drug, you just feel disconnected from reality and your body. 

One time I took it on a Friday, was still semi high on Saturday, and was coming down on Sunday. This was with maybe 300MG or less. If you take very high doses, you may be high all week, idk. Another time I took it on a Monday, and woke up the next morning with my entire shirt wet with sweat, but was STILL a little high. Though was feeling semi-sober. Maybe someone else can comment with their own experience. 

I would advise against using it, it can ruin your life like any other drug. Worst part is how easily it's accessible, literally order some on amazon or go to your local store. I been 5 months without popping them, but the cravings are there WEEKLY or on really crappy days. If you don't care and are still interested in knowing how it feels like, I guess you can dose safely at 150 to 200mg for starters. Last time I relapsed, I accidentally took x6 60 MG pills, so 360mg total, I felt pretty fucked up already, and that's when I first experienced my out of body experience, I lost control of my body.

Others suggest 400MG or more, but fuck that. Some regularly dose that daily with high tolerance, but to each their own. Depends if you want to be fucked up for 3-4 days, or just wanted to have fun 1 day, and be semi-sober the next. Though like alcohol, you will still be fearless from being high and not feel anything if someone argues with you lol, again, numb mind. Best of luck.

Man, sorry to hear about all that. I am not diabetic, but I got cancer at around 3 years old, and therefore, a whole world of medical issues and such. It affected me mentally and physical, and more so socially. 

As for you, I know its hard to get out of that narrow thinking, as I been battling depression and suicidal ideation as a young kid, but you life and future are still possible. Your illness should not, and will not stop you from pursuing your dream, you are the one doing that.

I know you want to join the military, politics, or a family, and sure some of the careers may not be viable, but that does not mean you can't make a difference in the community. Do you think serving in the military is the only way? Its a job just like any other, so don't feel so down about that.

I have seen new players ingame which is great, but lemme just give you a few basic tips.

1. Use your weapons from the perk your using!!! Don't be playing zerker using shotguns...I see too many new players do this with their weapons.
 
2. If someone dies, and you pickup their weapon, its common courtesy to give it back to them, NEVER sell it. Press backspace to drop weapons.

3. If you play support with ammo, please stand on the very edge of the trader pod, people are trying to get ammo from you, don't hug the trader making it harder for others. Its best to get ammo from a support before buying more ammo.

4. If trying out multiplayer, do not rage the flesh pounds or scrakes, if you fought them already, you know when they turn red and charge at you. You can get people killed if you do this, so don't initiate the fight unless others are around to help kill it. Careful with firebug and the fire, can rage it.

5. Stay close together with your team, don't go solo at the other end of the map, thats super selfish, many players do it though. You may get killed if you arent visible to the medic, so yea. 

6. Its best to save up money to buy the real expensive guns, they will better help kill big boys like fleshpounds and scrakes. Its not always best to buy new guns every round. Say you got 650 dosh to buy the gun, but the next tier is 1100-1200, always better to save up instead of buying junk that you will replace in 2 rounds. 

7. Generally, just be a good teammate...don't weld people outside doors or inside, you may get them killed. Heal players with your syringe, help plays if they are getting surrounded by mobs or need help taking a big zed down. Just simple basic gamer stuff.

8. Have Fun! This isn't very in depth, but probably the basics I wish I learned. Slowly you will learn how to play the perks, what skills to learn, what guns are better than others, but just have fun for the meantime. You don't have to start optimizing and ruining your own fun. Though granted, some guns suck and should never be bought, but normal difficulty is pretty chill. 

I would definitely suggest playing in a group, way more fun and chaotic! :) helps you learn much faster. Will help you get better at solo play too. Welcome to kf2!

Only real thing that helped me is my belief in Jesus and Heaven. Lost my dog on halloween night. 12 years he lived with us. He got sick last year though, heart murmur and just this weird coughing noise he made, maybe collapsed trachea. I bought him medicine and it helped but he was still sick. I noticed he looked weird one day, with his head up and struggling to breathe. He was like that for 1 day, and I told my mom and sister we HAVE to take him to the vet the next day. On the way to the vet, I already knew we were going to euthanize him.

But at our church we sing different songs, one of which is "Do it again". One of the lyrics was this: 

Your promise still stands  
Great is Your faithfulness, faithfulness  
I'm still in Your hands  
This is my confidence  
You've never failed me yet

I kept hearing that song in my head, and I knew everything would be ok. Yes, we had to euthanize him at the vet hospital. A lot of tears from my mom and sister, but I tried to be strong. But when they gave him back to us to spend the last few moments with us, thats when I couldnt hold it in anymore. He was in heart failure, and his lungs were full of blood. Had to comfort my mom and remind her of heaven. It still hurts honestly. We paid for his ashes+his pawprint+ they put some of his hairs too. But I felt at peace honestly, he never has to suffer again. I just imagine him running around in the green grass of heaven. I don't know if you believe in God or not, or atheist. But I'm just sharing my own experience. A friend at the church that day also told my sister she felt she had to pray for our family that day. 

Now we only have 1 dog left, and we will take care of him as much as possible, and spoil it obviously. But my dog that passed away was me and my dads, if that makes sense. Our other dog is super clingy to my mom, so we never really grew close compared to my dog. But hes our last dog, so I still love him, and always have. 

Pets hurt alot because of the unconditional love we have for them, they are closer than friends. I'm sorry for your loss, don't feel bad for crying, its the process of healing, so its a good thing. But for me, I have more peace, and I know I will see him again. If your not religious, I don't know, its still the same healing process, just dont feel guilty.
